lines.text: You'd never pay someone to sit in your car.
This guy owes four thousand rupees for it.
Rewind one year.
Arjun drives. Priya, Rohan and Sharma ji ride along.
Petrol gets split every Friday, on whatever's in the glovebox.
Week one. One napkin. Rohan owes two hundred. Clean.
Month two. Tolls, parking, and Sharma ji's samosas.
Month six. The glovebox physically will not close.
So Arjun, the engineer, builds a spreadsheet.
Twelve tabs. Colour coded. A formula for samosas.
One error. Nobody opens it again.
Back to napkins. Except now Sharma ji does the maths.
Which brings us to today.
The final napkin says Arjun owes Sharma ji four thousand.
For driving him. In Arjun's own car.
Moral: a carpool survives traffic. It doesn't survive napkin maths.
So the four moved the money into an app.
Every petrol bill goes into settle costs. The app splits it.
The roster rotates the driving too, so Arjun gets mornings off.
And the glovebox? It closes now.
Sharma ji still pays in samosas. Now the guard gets one too.
If your carpool still runs on napkins, Sahyatri does the maths.
Link in bio.
